note: Original evaluation briefs for the in-app director, written for Motion Studio (not taken from any third-party gallery). Each covers one category of code-driven motion. Inputs are pre-filled so runs are non-interactive.

briefs.brief: A 12-second square UI motion loop for a note-taking app called Margin. One rounded rectangle never leaves the frame: it is a 'New note' button, then a loading ring, then a checkmark, then a slider the cursor drags to 80%, then a tab bar whose indicator glides between three tabs, then the button again. Warm off-white canvas, black components, one green accent (#1f9d55), Geist. 120 BPM: something changes on every beat.

A 10-second vertical kinetic-type manifesto for a bike repair co-op called Spoke & Hub: 'Fix it. / Ride it. / Pass it on.' Each phrase is set huge and travels into the next by a match on a shared letter. Ink black on newsprint cream, one red accent. Cuts on downbeats at 100 BPM.

A 12-second data story for a solar startup, Lumen Grid: monthly household bill drops from $142 to $38 after install. A bar chart draws itself, the last bar is highlighted, then the number $104 saved per month lands as big type and the chart collapses into the logo dot. Dark slate canvas, one amber accent, IBM Plex Mono for numbers.

Explain in 14 seconds how a webhook relay called Hookline works: an event leaves a payment service, Hookline queues it, retries twice on failure, and delivers it to three customer endpoints. One packet travels the whole film. Light canvas, hairline strokes, one violet accent.

A 12-second launch spot for a CLI called tidy that formats SQL. A terminal types `tidy query.sql`, the messy query snaps into a clean layout line by line, and the closing card reads 'tidy — SQL that reads like prose'. Charcoal editor, one lime accent, JetBrains Mono.

A 10-second square visual for a lo-fi single called 'Night Bus' by Paper Lanterns: a single circle breathes with the kick, the title type sits beside it in a serif italic, and the circle becomes the 'o' in 'Lanterns' at the end. Deep navy, one warm orange accent, 84 BPM.

An 8-second identity sting for an architecture studio called Fold: a square folds along a diagonal into a triangle, the triangle unfolds into the letter F, and the wordmark resolves. Concrete gray, one blue accent, crisp springs with almost no overshoot.

A 12-second vertical feature film for a budgeting app called Penny: a phone shows the home screen, the cursor drags a spending-limit slider past its maximum and it springs back to $500, a toggle turns on 'Round-ups', and a toast confirms 'Saved $14 this week'. Off-white, one teal accent.

A 10-second product reveal for a ceramic pour-over dripper called Still: the camera glides around a softly lit 3D object on a matte floor, focus racks from the rim to the logo, and the end card holds the name with a one-line promise 'Slow is the point.' Warm stone palette, no saturated colors.

A 12-second 4:5 photo story for a bakery called Rise: three photo cards (dough, oven, loaf — use shapes as stand-ins if no images exist) each push in slowly, the next card grows out of a detail of the previous one, and the end card reads 'Baked before you wake'. Flour white, one rust accent.
